pr_title: Add various OBJ functions as callbacks
pr_body:
This enables providers to register new OIDs in the same libcrypto instance
as is used by the application.

Fixes #15624
pr_comments:
I'm going to go out on a limb and show how ignorant I am about providers. 

Is there a reason these need to be done as callbacks?  Is there a problem with just calling `OBJ_add_sigid()` directly instead of using the callbacks?

> Is there a reason these need to be done as callbacks? Is there a problem with just calling OBJ_add_sigid() directly instead of using the callbacks?

It is entirely possible for the provider and the application to be using different instances of libcrypto - or even entirely different versions. For example the application could be statically linked and the provider is dynamically linked. Or the application is dynamically linked against some future OpenSSL 4.0, but the provider is linked against 3.0. In such cases if the provider calls `OBJ_add_sigid()` directly then it will only impact the provider's own instance of libcrypto and not the application's. If the application then attempts to use an OID registered by the provider it won't be found.
It's also possible to write a provider entirely without linking against libcrypto *at all*. This is actually the case with our own FIPS provider.

> It's also possible to write a provider entirely without linking against libcrypto _at all_. This is actually the case with our own FIPS provider.

YES!  I've noticed this!  Might I ask why it does not link with libcrypto? Is this some kind of FIPS requirement?

> YES! I've noticed this! Might I ask why it does not link with libcrypto? Is this some kind of FIPS requirement?

Yes. Once we've entered the module boundary we mustn't leave it to go off and do stuff we need to do along the way of fulfilling a crypto request. Doing so would mean we'd have to the pull the whole of libcrypto into the module boundary and validate the whole thing. We don't want to do that :-)

> Yes. Once we've entered the module boundary we mustn't leave it to go off and do stuff we need to do along the way of fulfilling a crypto request. Doing so would mean we'd have to the pull the whole of libcrypto into the module boundary and validate the whole thing. We don't want to do that :-)

Thank you for the explanation!!  I hate taking up your time with silly points so one last thing and I'll be quiet ... 

Isn't calling a callback leaving the boundary?

> Isn't calling a callback leaving the boundary?

Good question. Yes, technically it is, but you are allowed to do so for some OS/platform type services. For example its ok for us to link against libc and use libc calls without having to validate all of libc. Where we provide such upcalls we would have to be able to justify that they wouldn't impact the validation in any way because they aren't cryptographically relevant.
Ok, I think I understand.  Thank you so much for your explanations and time.  I really appreciate it.

I had to look up 1.3.6.1.4.1.16604.998877...  I had no idea we have an OID arc!

Neither did I. I needed some test OIDs and was going to make something up. Then I thought we really ought to have our own arc for such things.....I don't suppose we already have one.....I'll go check....oh we do!!!!

> This is good enough

I _just slightly_ disagree. Please consider my comment above.
Re the OID arc, we really should fix the contact...  It's currently Ben Laurie, he hasn't been part of the OpenSSL group since, oh I dunno...  eons?

issue_context.title: Should we add an upcall for registering a sig alg OID?
comments: IMO: we should.  Should we do it for 3.0?  I think not.
I would rather go for a mechanism to make sigalgs directly fetchable. In my view, this would be an interim measure.

>  In my view, this would be an interim measure.

Yes - my suggestion was intended as an interim measure that we can do relatively easily now before the fuller solution that you outline is implemented in some future release.

Yeah, if it's clearly marked as an interim measure, I'm on board with that.

What troubles me is that such interim measures often become not so interim, and I worry about putting that into the provider side...  it's at the same level as adding a function that gets immediately deprecated.

So, one last question to help me decide: do you believe that there will be new sigalgs appearing anytime soon, i.e. before 3.1?
And just for the base of comparison, I plan on a serious introduction of the fuller solution as soon as possible, at the latest directly after we release of 3.0.0.  I believe it should be part of 3.1.
My thinking is that as long as our internal libcrypto table (`crypto/objects/obj_xref.h`) can be assumed to be sufficient, there's really no need to introduce any updating functionality of that table to providers.
Just to add a bit of context, I'm trying to write a 3.0.0 provider with signature algorithms that OpenSSL doesn't know about.

> do you believe that there will be new sigalgs appearing anytime soon, i.e. before 3.1?

My assumption is that @baentsch and others on the oqs project would be interested in this prior to 3.1 - and we've just heard that @anhu is doing the same. So, yes, I think this would be useful for people before 3.1

> So, yes, I think this would be useful for people before 3.1

Okie.

review_comments: OBJ_add_sigid() does not check whether there is already such triplet registered. That means we might get the same triplets registered multiple times if a provider is loaded/unloaded multiple times. Do we care or should we do a similar check as done below for OBJ_create?
Yes. I think we care. Fixed.
